definitions.guidelines: Use these tools to manage pages in Concrete CMS. You can list, create, read and update pages. A page made with create_page is unpublished: a person publishes it from Page Versions. Moving and deleting pages are not available yet (they return with approvals), so say so instead of trying another tool. Always check permissions before modifying content.

tools.name: list_pages

properties.name: limit
properties.description: Maximum number of pages to return (1-100)

properties.name: parentID
properties.description: Filter by parent page ID (direct children only unless includeDescendants=true)

properties.name: parentPath
properties.description: Filter by parent page path (e.g., "/newsroom/press-releases"). Use instead of parentID when you have a path.

properties.name: includeDescendants
properties.description: If true, include ALL pages under the parent (recursive). If false, only direct children. Default: false

properties.name: pageType
properties.description: Filter by page type handle (e.g., "page", "blog_entry")

tools.name: add_block_to_page_area
tools.description: Add a new block to a specific page area. blockType must be the handle of the block type the user asked for. Never substitute a different type (for example, do not use "content" when the user asked for an HTML block). Common handles: content = rich text (formatted text, headings, paragraphs); html = raw HTML, for markup that must be kept exactly as written; image = a single image; file = a link to a downloadable file; page_list = a list of pages; autonav = a navigation menu; youtube or video = an embedded video; google_map = a map; form = a Concrete form; accordion, faq, feature = structured content blocks. If the requested type does not exist or you are unsure of its handle, say so instead of choosing another.

properties.name: pageID
properties.description: ID of the page that contains the target area

properties.name: areaHandle
properties.description: Handle of the area (for example: "Main")

properties.name: blockType
properties.description: Handle of the block type the user asked for, used exactly as requested ("content" = rich text, "html" = raw HTML, "image", "file", "page_list", ...). Do not pick a different type.

properties.name: value
properties.description: Block data payload matching the block type fields

definitions.guidelines: Use these tools to search for and inspect blocks across the site. WORKFLOW: First use search_blocks_by_type to find blocks and get their blockID, pageID, and areaHandle. For blocks INSIDE CONTAINERS: Look for area handles with ' : ' delimiter (e.g., '12704 : Column 1'). Use list_container_blocks(containerBlockID) to see all nested blocks. Then use get_block_controller_data with blockID, pageID, and the full areaHandle (including container ID) to see the actual content. This is more efficient than querying each page individually when looking for specific block types.

definitions.guidelines: Use these tools to manage page attributes in Concrete CMS. You can list existing page attributes, get detailed information about specific attributes, create new page attributes with various types (text, select, boolean, etc.), update select attribute options, and set attribute values on pages. When setting page attributes, you can identify pages by ID, path, or name (fuzzy matching supported). For select attributes, option values are matched case-insensitively. Always check that attribute handles don't already exist before creating new ones. Attribute handles should be lowercase with underscores (e.g., 'nav_group', 'custom_field').

definitions.guidelines: Use these tools to manage attribute sets in Concrete CMS. Attribute sets organize attributes into logical groups in the CMS interface. definitions.guidelines: Use these tools to work with topic trees in Concrete CMS. Topic trees are hierarchical taxonomies used for categorization (e.g., Specialisms, Industries, Categories). You can list available topic trees, browse their structure, search for specific topics by name, and get detailed information about topics including their children. Topic trees are used both directly in custom entities (like People) and through Concrete's attribute system (topics-type attributes on pages/users/files). definitions.guidelines:
Version Management Guidelines:

CRITICAL SAFETY PROTOCOL:
Before ANY destructive edit (update content, delete blocks, cleanup HTML):
1. Create a draft version first (create_page_draft)
2. Make changes in that draft version
3. User previews the draft
4. User explicitly approves OR discards

WORKFLOW:
- list_page_versions: Show version history
- create_page_draft: Create safe sandbox for edits
- [User previews at /page?cvID=X]
- Publishing a version is done by a person in the CMS; this assistant cannot publish
- discard_draft_version: Revert if rejected

NEVER edit content directly in approved/active versions!
ALWAYS offer a preview before destructive operations!

When user says "revert to version X" or "go back" or "undo" → list versions, then tell them a person must publish the earlier version in the CMS; this assistant cannot publish

definitions.guidelines: Use these tools to manage attributes and attribute sets in Concrete CMS. You can list existing attributes, create new page/user/file attributes, get attribute details, and set attribute values on pages. You can also manage attribute sets: list them, create/delete sets, and add/remove attributes from sets. When setting page attributes, you can identify pages by ID, path, or name (fuzzy matching supported). For select attributes, option values are matched case-insensitively. Always check that attribute handles don't already exist before creating new ones. Attribute handles should be lowercase with underscores (e.g., 'nav_group', 'custom_field'). Attribute sets help organize attributes in the CMS interface.

offered.guidelines:
Toolkit: PagesToolkit
Use these tools to manage pages in Concrete CMS. You can list, create, read and update pages. A page made with create_page is unpublished: a person publishes it from Page Versions. Moving and deleting pages are not available yet (they return with approvals), so say so instead of trying another tool. Always check permissions before modifying content.

Use these tools to search for and inspect blocks across the site. WORKFLOW: First use search_blocks_by_type to find blocks and get their blockID, pageID, and areaHandle. For blocks INSIDE CONTAINERS: Look for area handles with ' : ' delimiter (e.g., '12704 : Column 1'). Use list_container_blocks(containerBlockID) to see all nested blocks. Then use get_block_controller_data with blockID, pageID, and the full areaHandle (including container ID) to see the actual content. This is more efficient than querying each page individually when looking for specific block types.

Toolkit: FilesToolkit
Use these tools to manage files in Concrete CMS. Use resolve_file_id_from_path before assigning image/file references: Concrete URL folders like /application/files/9215/0056/1806/... are storage segments, not the fID. Never infer fID from URL path numbers. Use create_file_folder to create folders in the file manager, and move_file_to_folder to organize files into folders.
Use these tools to retrieve information about users in Concrete CMS. You can list users, get user details, and check the current user. User creation and modification should be done with caution.

Toolkit: PageAttributesToolkit
Use these tools to manage page attributes in Concrete CMS. You can list existing page attributes, get detailed information about specific attributes, create new page attributes with various types (text, select, boolean, etc.), update select attribute options, and set attribute values on pages. When setting page attributes, you can identify pages by ID, path, or name (fuzzy matching supported). For select attributes, option values are matched case-insensitively. Always check that attribute handles don't already exist before creating new ones. Attribute handles should be lowercase with underscores (e.g., 'nav_group', 'custom_field').

Toolkit: UserAttributesToolkit
Use these tools to manage user attributes in Concrete CMS. You can list existing user attributes, get detailed information about specific attributes, create new user attributes with various types (text, select, boolean, etc.), update select attribute options, and set attribute values on users. When setting user attributes, you can identify users by ID, username, or email. For select attributes, option values are matched case-insensitively. Always check that attribute handles don't already exist before creating new ones. Attribute handles should be lowercase with underscores (e.g., 'department', 'job_title').

Toolkit: FileAttributesToolkit
Use these tools to manage file attributes in Concrete CMS. You can list existing file attributes, get detailed information about specific attributes, create new file attributes with various types (text, select, boolean, etc.), update select attribute options, and set attribute values on files. When setting file attributes, you can identify files by ID or filename. For select attributes, option values are matched case-insensitively. Always check that attribute handles don't already exist before creating new ones. Attribute handles should be lowercase with underscores (e.g., 'copyright_holder', 'license_type').

Toolkit: AttributeSetsToolkit
Use these tools to manage attribute sets in Concrete CMS. Attribute sets organize attributes into logical groups in the CMS interface. You can list existing sets, create new sets, delete sets (attributes are not deleted, just ungrouped), add attributes to sets, and remove attributes from sets. All tools support three categories: 'collection' (for pages), 'user' (for user attributes), and 'file' (for file attributes). The category parameter defaults to 'collection'. When working with sets, you can identify them by their handle (lowercase with underscores).

Toolkit: TopicsToolkit
Use these tools to work with topic trees in Concrete CMS. Topic trees are hierarchical taxonomies used for categorization (e.g., Specialisms, Industries, Categories). You can list available topic trees, browse their structure, search for specific topics by name, and get detailed information about topics including their children. Topic trees are used both directly in custom entities (like People) and through Concrete's attribute system (topics-type attributes on pages/users/files). When working with topics, you can identify them by handle/name or by treeNodeID.

Toolkit: PeopleToolkit
Use these tools to manage People in the Katalysis Pro system. People are a custom entity (not pages or users) with properties like name, job title, email, and relationships to Places, Specialisms, and Topics. Specialisms and Topics are topic tree nodes stored in junction tables (KatalysisPeopleSpecialism, KatalysisPeopleTopic). When updating specialisms or topics, provide an array of topic node IDs. Use the Topics toolkit to search for topic IDs by name. People can be identified by ID, name (fuzzy matching), or email.

Toolkit: VersionsToolkit
Version Management Guidelines:

CRITICAL SAFETY PROTOCOL:
Before ANY destructive edit (update content, delete blocks, cleanup HTML):
1. Create a draft version first (create_page_draft)
2. Make changes in that draft version
3. User previews the draft
4. User explicitly approves OR discards

WORKFLOW:
- list_page_versions: Show version history
- create_page_draft: Create safe sandbox for edits
- [User previews at /page?cvID=X]
- Publishing a version is done by a person in the CMS; this assistant cannot publish
- discard_draft_version: Revert if rejected

NEVER edit content directly in approved/active versions!
ALWAYS offer a preview before destructive operations!

When user says "revert to version X" or "go back" or "undo" → list versions, then tell them a person must publish the earlier version in the CMS; this assistant cannot publish
